learningObjectives.title: The internet and the world wide web

questions.q: Which statement best describes the World Wide Web (WWW)?
options: A worldwide collection of interconnected computer networks
A collection of websites and web pages that are accessed using the internet
A protocol used to transfer files between servers
A device that joins two separate networks together
questions.explain: The WWW is the collection of websites and web pages, whereas the internet is the underlying worldwide network infrastructure used to access them.

questions.q: A user types a website address into their browser, but the browser needs the site's numerical IP address before it can connect. Which system supplies this?
options: The Domain Name System (DNS)
A persistent cookie
The HTTPS protocol
A proxy firewall
questions.explain: The DNS translates the human-readable domain name into the corresponding IP address so the browser can locate the web server.

questions.q: In the URL https://www.example.com/page.html, which part is the protocol?
options: https
www.example.com
/page.html
example
questions.explain: A URL is made up of the protocol (https), the domain name (www.example.com) and the web page/file name (/page.html).

questions.q: What does the 's' in HTTPS indicate compared with HTTP?
options: The data transferred between browser and server is encrypted
The web pages will load at a faster speed
The website is stored on more than one server
The site is guaranteed to be a search engine
questions.explain: HTTPS is the secure version of HTTP, encrypting transmitted data (typically using SSL/TLS) so it cannot be easily read if intercepted.

questions.q: Which of the following is a function of a web browser?
options: Rendering HTML in order to display web pages
Translating domain names into IP addresses
Hosting websites so other users can access them
Automatically encrypting all internet traffic
questions.explain: A browser's main role is to request web pages and render the returned HTML into the page the user sees.

questions.q: When a user enters a URL, which of these happens first?
options: The browser sends the URL to a DNS to obtain the IP address
The web server sends the HTML back to the browser
The browser renders the HTML into a web page
A cookie is stored on the user's device
questions.explain: The IP address must be obtained from the DNS before the browser can request the page from the web server.

questions.q: What is a cookie in the context of web browsing?
options: A small text file stored on a user's computer by a website
A program that translates HTML into a web page
A type of malware that damages stored files
A protocol used to transfer web pages securely
questions.explain: Cookies are small text files placed on a user's device to store data such as preferences or login details.

questions.q: Which statement about a session cookie is correct?
options: It is deleted when the browser is closed and is not stored permanently
It remains stored until it expires or is manually deleted
It encrypts the data sent to the web server
It translates a URL into an IP address
questions.explain: A session cookie is temporary and is removed when the browser session ends, unlike a persistent cookie.

questions.q: An online shop remembers the items a user left in their basket across several days and separate visits. Which is being used?
options: A persistent cookie stored on the user's device
A session cookie deleted when the browser closes
A DNS record on the web server
An SSL certificate
questions.explain: A persistent cookie survives between browsing sessions, allowing the basket contents to be remembered over several days.

questions.q: Which statement best describes digital currency?
options: Currency that exists only in electronic form and has no physical form
Physical coins and banknotes issued by a central bank
A cookie used to store a user's payment card details
A protocol used to make secure online payments
questions.explain: Digital currency has no notes or coins; it exists purely electronically and is used in transactions.

questions.q: Which statement best describes cryptocurrency?
options: It uses cryptography to track transactions and is not regulated by a central bank
It is controlled and regulated by a country's central bank
It exists as physical tokens exchanged between users
It can only be used to purchase web hosting services
questions.explain: Unlike traditional (central-bank) digital currency, cryptocurrency is decentralised and uses cryptography to secure and track transactions.

questions.q: What is a blockchain?
options: A decentralised digital ledger that records transactions in linked blocks
A central database controlled by a single bank
A type of cookie used during online banking
A firewall that blocks unauthorised transactions
questions.explain: A blockchain is a decentralised, time-stamped digital ledger in which transactions are stored in blocks that are chained together.

questions.q: Why is it very difficult to alter a transaction already recorded on a blockchain?
options: Each block is linked to previous blocks, so changing one block affects all the blocks that follow
Each block is stored on a single central server that no one can access
Each block is encrypted using the user's account password
Transactions are automatically deleted after each session
questions.explain: Because blocks are cryptographically linked in sequence, tampering with one block invalidates every subsequent block, making changes easy to detect.

questions.q: What is a brute-force attack?
options: Repeatedly trying different combinations in order to crack a password
Flooding a server with requests until it can no longer respond
Redirecting a user to a fake website using malicious code
Sending fraudulent emails to trick users into giving details
questions.explain: A brute-force attack systematically tries many possible combinations to guess a password or key.

questions.q: What is the aim of a Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack?
options: To flood a server with requests so that legitimate users cannot access it
To guess a user's password by trying many combinations
To encrypt a user's files and demand a payment
To trick a user into revealing personal details by email
questions.explain: A DDoS attack overwhelms a server with traffic from many computers so that genuine users are denied the service.

questions.q: Which statement describes pharming?
options: Malicious code redirects a user to a fake website without their knowledge
Fraudulent emails trick a user into giving away personal details
A network is flooded with traffic to make it unavailable
Software secretly records a user's key presses
questions.explain: Pharming uses malicious code (for example on a device or DNS) to redirect users to a fake website even when the correct address is entered.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes phishing?
options: Sending fake emails that appear legitimate to trick users into revealing personal data
Redirecting users to fake sites using malicious code on a device
Recording key presses to capture passwords secretly
Overloading a server with an excessive number of requests
questions.explain: Phishing uses fraudulent emails or messages disguised as legitimate ones to lure users into disclosing confidential information.

questions.q: A user finds that all of their files have been encrypted and a message on screen demands a payment before the files will be unlocked. Which type of malware is this?
options: Ransomware
Adware
Spyware
Worm
questions.explain: Ransomware encrypts a victim's files and demands a payment (a ransom) in exchange for restoring access.

questions.q: What does spyware do?
options: Secretly gathers information by monitoring user activity, such as key presses
Displays unwanted advertisements on the user's screen
Replicates itself to spread across a network
Encrypts files and demands a ransom to release them
questions.explain: Spyware covertly monitors and records user activity, such as keystrokes, and sends the data back to the attacker.

questions.q: A company wants to monitor the traffic between its internal network and the internet and block unauthorised access. Which security measure should it use?
options: A firewall
A persistent cookie
A DNS server
A brute-force attack
questions.explain: A firewall monitors incoming and outgoing traffic between a network and the internet, blocking traffic that does not meet its rules.
